text: The pig digestive system is a tube starting at the mouth and finishing at the rectum. The mouth (36 teeth) opens into the pharynx, the common passage for both feed and air. The esophagus is a muscular tube moving swallowed feed to the stomach. The stomach has only one compartment (pigs are monogastric) of about 7.5 liters; the spleen is attached to the stomach. The small intestine can reach 18 m long. The cecum sits between the small and large intestine. The large intestine is near 5 m long, followed by the rectum and anus. The liver has 5 lobes and one gall bladder; a healthy liver should be firm and soft with a homogeneous dark brown-red color. Ducts from the liver and pancreas empty into the small intestine.
